name: INA3221 3-channel current & voltage monitor
description: Texas Instruments three-channel current and voltage monitor with an I2C interface: for each channel it measures the voltage across a shunt resistor (±163.8 mV, 40 µV per count) and the bus voltage at the load (0–26 V, 8 mV per count). Runs on 2.7–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit INA3221 breakout (#6062, 15-pin header: VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, VIN3+, VIN3-, VIN2+, VIN2-, VIN1+, VIN1-, WRN, CRI, TC, VALID, VPU) with 0.05 Ω shunts (about ±3.2 A per channel), I2C address 0x40 (0x41 with the Addr jumper closed).
eli5: Watches three power wires at once and tells your board how many volts and milliamps each one carries.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Chip supply, 2.7–5.5 V; also sets the I2C logic level (3.3 V recommended)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground, shared with the microcontroller and the measured supplies

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up to VCC on the board)

pins.name: VIN3+
pins.description: Channel 3 shunt high side: from the supply being measured (0–26 V). Never to a GPIO.

pins.name: VIN3-
pins.description: Channel 3 shunt low side: to the load's + lead (bus voltage is measured here, 0–26 V). Never to a GPIO.

pins.name: VIN2+
pins.description: Channel 2 shunt high side: from the supply being measured (0–26 V). Never to a GPIO.

pins.name: VIN2-
pins.description: Channel 2 shunt low side: to the load's + lead (bus voltage is measured here, 0–26 V). Never to a GPIO.

pins.name: VIN1+
pins.description: Channel 1 shunt high side: from the supply being measured (0–26 V). Never to a GPIO.

pins.name: VIN1-
pins.description: Channel 1 shunt low side: to the load's + lead (bus voltage is measured here, 0–26 V). Never to a GPIO.

pins.name: WRN
pins.description: Warning alert output (open-drain, active low, 10 kΩ pull-up to VCC), not needed for basic use

pins.name: CRI
pins.description: Critical alert output (open-drain, active low, 10 kΩ pull-up to VCC), not needed for basic use

pins.name: TC
pins.description: Timing-control alert output (open-drain, active low, 10 kΩ pull-up to VCC), not needed for basic use

pins.name: VALID
pins.description: Power-valid output (open-drain, 10 kΩ pull-up to VPU), not needed for basic use

pins.name: VPU
pins.description: Pull-up supply for VALID: link to VCC only if you use VALID

supplierQuery: Adafruit INA3221 triple power monitor breakout 6062
buildNotes: Each shunt goes in series with its load: supply + to VINn+, VINn- to the load's + lead, and every measured supply's ground to the same GND as the microcontroller.

VIN pins may carry up to 26 V: never connect them to a GPIO. With the 0.05 Ω shunts each channel reads up to about ±3.2 A (163.8 mV full scale); carry load current through the screw terminals, not the thin header pins or breadboard jumpers.
Shunt registers 01h/03h/05h and bus registers 02h/04h/06h hold a signed value in bits 15..3: shift right by 3, then 40 µV (shunt) or 8 mV (bus) per count. Current = shunt voltage / 0.05 Ω.
Manufacturer ID FEh reads 5449h and Die ID FFh reads 3220h: a quick wiring check. Default address 0x40; close the Addr jumper for 0x41.
An unused channel reads 0; VPU only needs wiring (to VCC) if you use the VALID output.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ina3221 import INA3221

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = INA3221(i2c)  # address 0x40, 0.05 ohm shunts
while True:
    for ch in (1, 2, 3):
        v, i = sensor.read(ch)
        print('CH%d V=%.3fV I=%.1fmA' % (ch, v, i))
    time.sleep(1)
